domain_label: Content Engineering — High-Quality Flashcard Formulation (books to cards)
purpose: A method for turning understood source material into flashcards that a spaced-repetition scheduler can grade honestly: how to apply Wozniak's Twenty Rules and the minimum-information principle, when to reach for cloze deletion, image occlusion or a picture over text, which Anki note template each fact wants, and how to run the bad-card taxonomy (interference, sets, enumerations, overloaded, orphan, undated) as a deck-level lint gate with its documented fixes — while carrying the source-honesty (verbatim rule text is snippet-reconstructed this session, not fetched) inside the cards themselves.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the source pages for Wozniak's Twenty Rules and the Anki manual were 403-blocked this session, so rule wording is reconstructed from search snippets and verbatim mirrors, not fetched; the rules' ORDER-BY-IMPORTANCE and the numbered rules (1,2,4,5,17,18,19,20) are snippet-confirmed, the remaining positions follow canonical article order at high confidence
the target authoring tool is Anki (its note types, cloze syntax {{c1::...}} and native Image Occlusion since 23.10 are the concrete template surface); the principles are tool-independent
exclusions: the scheduling algorithm itself (SM-2/FSRS intervals, ease, review timing) — that belongs to the spaced-repetition specialist; this KB stops at what makes a single card and a deck well-formed

book decomposition mechanics (TOC parsing, unit/term/claim/edge extraction, Bloom laddering, prerequisite graph vs flat units) — that is the sibling book-decomposition KB; this KB consumes its claims/edges but does not derive them
export/tooling plumbing (.apkg build, AnkiConnect) beyond naming it as the compile target
asserting verbatim rule text or an Anki manual note-type list as fact where only a search snippet, not the fetched page, was available this session

competency_questions.question: Why must comprehension precede memorization, and what does a card built on un-understood text cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites Wozniak Rules 1-3 (do not learn if you do not understand; learn before you memorize; build on the basics) and states that memorizing un-understood text wastes time and yields worthless, orphan knowledge

competency_questions.question: What is the minimum-information principle and why does the scheduler need it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states one card = one atomic fact (Rule 4), explains that the scheduler grades a single memory trace so simple items are scheduled accurately and fail independently, and notes Rule 17 permits redundancy (the same fact from several angles as separate simple items)

competency_questions.question: When is cloze deletion the right form, and what are its quality guardrails?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer names cloze as Rule 5 (easy and effective, fastest text-to-item), gives the Anki {{c1::...}} / {{c2::...}} separate-card syntax, and states the guardrails: short deleted span, the remaining sentence must uniquely determine the answer, keep meaningful context not a bare list skeleton

competency_questions.question: When does an image or occlusion beat text, and how is image occlusion related to cloze?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states Rule 8 (graphic deletion is as good as cloze), that Anki Image Occlusion (native since 23.10) is a special case of cloze on image regions, cites the picture-superiority effect / dual coding / multimedia principle, and gives the rule to use images when the knowledge is spatial/structural and drop decorative images (coherence principle)

competency_questions.question: Why are sets and enumerations hard, and what is the documented conversion chain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites Rule 9 (sets are virtually un-memorizable unless converted to enumerations) and Rule 10 (enumerations dealt with via cloze), gives the set -> enumeration -> per-element cloze chain, mentions overlapping clozes and Rule 7 mnemonics for stubborn orders

competency_questions.question: What is interference, why is it a whole-deck property, and how is it fought?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites Rule 11 (similar items become intractable), explains that interference is judged across the whole deck not per card, and lists fixes: optimize wording (Rule 12), add a context/category cue (Rule 16), add an explicit A-vs-B comparison card, or delete one item

competency_questions.question: Which Anki note template does a given fact want?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer maps fact shapes to templates: one-directional fact -> Basic; symmetric term/definition pair -> Basic (and reversed); some-reversible -> optional reversed; spelling/terminology -> type-in; embedded fact/enumeration -> Cloze; diagram/anatomy -> Image Occlusion, and flags which of these are snippet-confirmed vs training-knowledge

competency_questions.question: When is auto-reversing a card safe, and when does it manufacture interference?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states the rule: only auto-reverse when the back uniquely identifies the front; a reversed card whose question is a generic definition shared by several terms manufactures interference (Rule 11), so suppress the reverse or use optional-reversed

competency_questions.question: What are the documented bad-card patterns and their fixes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer enumerates the taxonomy (overloaded, set, enumeration, interference pair, ambiguous question, orphan, undated volatile fact) each with its Rule-anchored fix, and distinguishes snippet-confirmed fixes from common-practice ones

competency_questions.question: How is source and date honesty carried into every card?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer cites Rule 18 (provide sources) and Rule 19 (date-stamp volatile facts like statistics), states the house policy that each generated card carries its KB source id, and notes an undated volatile fact silently goes stale

competency_questions.question: What is an edge (relation) card and when is it well-formed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer reads the owner's 'edges' as concept-map propositions (A, relation, B), gives the card family (forward, reverse-if-unique, relation, cloze), ties it to Rule 13 (refer to other memories), and states an edge card is only well-formed once both endpoint term-cards exist

competency_questions.question: What deck-level lint gate must a card pass before it ships?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answer states the go/no-go: minimum-information (split overloaded), interference check across the whole deck, uniqueness on reversed cards, sets/enumerations converted, source+date stamped, prioritized (Rule 20), and every card traces to a claim/edge; a failure loops back to re-split/re-word

glossary.definition: Wozniak's Rule 4: formulate each item as simply as possible so it carries one atomic fact/relation; simple items are answered fast and scheduled accurately because the scheduler grades ONE memory trace, complex answers mean more independent things to forget. Complemented (not contradicted) by Rule 17, which welcomes the same fact from several angles as separate simple items.

Wozniak's Rule 5: a sentence with a hidden fragment the learner supplies; the fastest path from source text to good items. In Anki, {{c1::hidden}} marks the deletion; {{c2::...}}, {{c3::...}} on one note generate SEPARATE cards, and same-numbered clozes hide together. Guardrail: the deleted span is short and the remaining sentence must uniquely determine the answer.

Wozniak's Rule 8: occluding part of an image is 'as good as cloze deletion' (e.g. mask one region of an anatomy plate and ask for it). Anki implements it natively as the Image Occlusion note type since version 23.10 — a special case of cloze deletion on image regions, one card per mask (or hide-all/reveal-one). Pre-23.10 it was the third-party Image Occlusion Enhanced add-on.

Wozniak's Rule 11: similar items confuse each other and even the simplest item can become intractable if it resembles another. It is a WHOLE-DECK property (a card can be fine alone yet interfere with a later one), fought by optimizing wording (Rule 12), adding a category/context cue (Rule 16), adding an explicit A-vs-B comparison card, or deleting one item.

A set is an unordered collection ('name the members of X'), virtually un-memorizable unless converted into an enumeration (Rule 9). An enumeration is an ordered list, still hard if asked whole; deal with it via cloze deletion (Rule 10) — one blank per card, overlapping clozes so each element is cued by its neighbors, and mnemonics (Rule 7) for stubborn orders.

The owner's 'edges' read as concept-map propositions (Novak & Canas): a triple (A, relation, B) such as (lidocaine, blocks, Na+ channels). Each triple yields a small card family — forward, reverse (only if unique, Rule 11), a relation card, and a cloze form — and is the Rule 13 'refer to other memories' mechanism in card form; well-formed only after both endpoint term-cards exist.

Pictures are remembered better than words (Paivio: ~twice as many images recalled as words after brief viewing); dual-coding theory attributes this to a visual PLUS a verbal trace (two retrieval paths), though recent work argues distinctiveness, not dual coding, is the mechanism — the effect is robust, the mechanism debated. Mayer's multimedia principle: words + pictures beat words alone, but decorative images add load (coherence principle).

Wozniak's Rules 18-19: annotate items with their source (so knowledge can be updated and its reliability judged) and date-stamp volatile facts such as statistics (so obsolescence is managed). House policy for this factory: every generated card carries its KB source id; an undated volatile fact silently goes stale.

The deck-level quality pass that applies the bad-card taxonomy's fixes before a card ships: split overloaded cards to atoms, convert sets -> enumerations -> clozes, run the interference check across the WHOLE deck, enforce uniqueness on reversed cards, and confirm each card carries a source and date; failures loop back to re-splitting or re-wording.

nodes.definition: Establish why a flashcard (a question, not a re-reading) is the unit at all: the testing effect — retrieval practice produces better delayed retention than restudying the same material (Roediger & Karpicke 2006, Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science; on delayed tests prior testing outperforms prior studying) [FACT - search snippet of the cited paper]. This is the empirical warrant the whole formulation method serves: every rule downstream exists to make retrieval accurate and unambiguous. It does NOT specify scheduling (intervals belong to the spaced-repetition specialist); it only justifies question-format items over passive notes.

included: the retrieval-practice-beats-restudy warrant and its citation
why items are question-format not passive notes
excluded: the scheduling intervals / ease / FSRS math
the per-rule formulation techniques

pros.claim: Anchoring the method in the testing effect gives every downstream rule a measured reason to exist rather than being style preference
pros.example: justifying the effort of splitting an overloaded card by the delayed-retention gain retrieval practice buys

cons.claim: The testing-effect evidence is generic to retrieval, not to any specific card format, so it warrants question-format but does not by itself rank cloze vs basic vs occlusion
cons.example: citing Roediger & Karpicke to defend a badly-worded card as if the format were validated

failure_modes: treating passive re-reading notes as study items because the retrieval warrant was skipped
over-claiming that a specific card format is 'proven' by generic testing-effect evidence
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the testing effect, cites Roediger & Karpicke 2006 as the warrant for question-format items, and separates it from scheduling
revisit_triggers: a controlled study on a specific card format (cloze vs occlusion) is located
the scheduling specialist changes what counts as a review item

base.update_signal: a format-specific retrieval study or a scheduling-boundary change updates the warrant

nodes.definition: Establish Wozniak's Twenty Rules of Formulating Knowledge (1999) as the governing rulebook, ordered by importance — the earlier rules are the most often violated or the most beneficial when complied with [FACT - snippet of the official article]. The first 16 rules revolve around making memories simple; rules 17-20 are meta-management (redundancy, sources, date-stamping, prioritize) [FACT - snippet]. HONESTY: the source pages (supermemo.com, super-memory.com, supermemo.guru) were 403-blocked this session, so verbatim rule wording is reconstructed from search snippets and verbatim mirrors; rules 1,2,4,5,17,18,19,20 were explicitly numbered in snippets and the remaining positions follow the canonical article order [ESTIMATE - high confidence; verbatim text an [UNKNOWN] blocker until fetch access exists]. This node is the index every other node cites a rule number against.

included: the verbatim-text-is-reconstructed honesty flag and which rules are snippet-numbered
excluded: the per-rule technique detail (each in its own node)
the Anki tooling that implements a rule

pros.claim: A single ordered canon lets every downstream node cite a rule number and inherit its priority weighting
pros.example: resolving a design dispute by the rule order (Rule 4 minimum-information outranks a stylistic preference)

cons.claim: Because verbatim text is snippet-reconstructed, presenting a rule's exact wording as canonical risks over-precision the fetch could correct
cons.example: quoting a rule heading word-for-word as authoritative when only its concept was snippet-confirmed

failure_modes: presenting reconstructed rule wording as verified verbatim text
losing the order-by-importance so a low-priority rule overrides a high-priority one
acceptance_tests: the canon is stated as ordered-by-importance, the first-16-simple / 17-20-meta split is given, and the verbatim-text-reconstructed / [UNKNOWN] blocker is flagged with the snippet-numbered rules named
revisit_triggers: fetch access to the official article lets verbatim text be confirmed
a rule's canonical position is corrected against the fetched source
a downstream node needs a rule not yet indexed

base.update_signal: fetch access confirms verbatim text or corrects a rule's canonical position

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rules 1-3 as the precondition for any card: do not learn if you do not understand (memorizing un-understood text costs huge time and the knowledge is worthless); learn before you memorize (build the overall picture first — pieces that fit one coherent structure memorize faster); build upon the basics (start simple, do not hesitate to memorize obvious basics, their cost is small) [FACT - snippets]. Operationally this is a reading/understanding pass BEFORE card compilation; a card cut from un-understood text is an orphan (see the bad-card taxonomy). It gates the whole pipeline: no atomic item, cloze or edge is well-formed if its source was not first understood.

included: the reading pass before card compilation
the link to the orphan-card failure
excluded: the atomic-split mechanics (Rule 4, its own node)
the memory-anchoring rules 13-15 that come after comprehension

pros.claim: Requiring comprehension first prevents the most expensive failure — rote cards for un-understood material that lapse forever
pros.example: reading the chapter and grasping the mechanism before clozing its equation, so the cloze is meaningful not magical

cons.claim: A hard comprehension gate can stall throughput when 'obvious basics' would have been cheap to memorize immediately (Rule 3 tempers this)
cons.example: refusing to card a simple term until a full mechanism is understood, when the basic term was safe to learn early

failure_modes: compiling cards from text the author does not understand, producing orphan rote junk
over-gating so cheap basic facts are withheld against Rule 3
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Rules 1-3, requires a comprehension/reading pass before card compilation, and links skipped comprehension to the orphan-card failure
revisit_triggers: an orphan-card lapse pattern traces to skipped comprehension
the book-decomposition KB changes what a 'unit' delivers to comprehension

base.update_signal: an orphan-lapse pattern or a unit-delivery change updates the comprehension gate

nodes.definition: Establish the core rule (Wozniak Rule 4): formulate each item as simply as possible — one card carries one atomic fact/relation. Simple items are answered fast and scheduled accurately because the scheduler grades a SINGLE memory trace, not a bundle; complex answers mean more independent things to forget and fail together [FACT on the principle per Rule 4 snippet; the per-item-scheduling rationale is a direct consequence, ESTIMATE-high]. The violation symptom is a chronically 'half-known' card whose grade is meaningless — the documented fix is to split. Rule 17 is the explicit complement, NOT a contradiction: the same fact from several angles is welcome as separate simple items. This is the principle cloze, occlusion, template choice and the bad-card lint all serve.

included: the half-known symptom and the Rule 17 redundancy complement
excluded: the mechanical split procedure (its own node)
the specific note-template that carries the atom

pros.claim: Atomic items give the scheduler a clean single trace to grade, so intervals track actual mastery instead of averaging a bundle
pros.example: splitting 'the heart has 4 chambers named X,Y,Z,W' into per-chamber items that each get their own accurate interval

cons.claim: Pushed to an extreme, atomization strips the disambiguating context a cloze needs, manufacturing interference or ambiguity
cons.example: clozing a bare '{{c1::3}}' with no context so it collides with every other numeric card in the deck

failure_modes: shipping an overloaded card whose single grade hides many traces
over-atomizing until items lose the context that keeps their answers unique
acceptance_tests: the analysis states one-card-one-atomic-fact (Rule 4), the single-trace scheduling rationale, the half-known symptom with split as the fix, and the Rule 17 redundancy complement
revisit_triggers: a half-known card pattern shows an atom is still overloaded
an over-atomization pattern traces to lost context
the scheduler changes how it grades multi-cloze notes

base.update_signal: an over/under-atomization pattern or a scheduler grading change updates the principle

nodes.definition: Operationalize Rule 4: take an overloaded item (many sub-answers, one grade) and split it into atoms, each a single subject-predicate-value, while keeping the redundancy Rule 17 blesses (the same fact from several angles as separate items). Procedure: identify each independently-testable fact in the answer; give each its own card; re-add a minimal disambiguating context cue (Rule 16) so no atom collides with a neighbor; keep source/date stamps on each child. The trade to watch: splitting too aggressively removes the context that made the answer unique, so the split must stop at the smallest item whose remaining stem still uniquely determines the answer.

included: the identify-facts / one-card-each / re-add-context split procedure
carrying source-date stamps to child cards
excluded: the interference diagnosis itself (its own node)
the enumeration-specific conversion chain

pros.claim: A repeatable split turns the vague 'this card is half-known' complaint into a concrete set of accurately-schedulable atoms
pros.example: breaking a 5-fact summary card into 5 atoms, each of which then earns its own honest interval

cons.claim: Splitting multiplies card count and, if context is dropped, can trade an overloaded card for an interference cluster
cons.example: five split atoms that all read '{{c1::...}}' with identical stems and now swap answers

failure_modes: leaving a residual overloaded atom that is still a bundle
dropping the disambiguating cue during the split and creating interference
acceptance_tests: the method identifies each independently-testable fact, gives each its own card with a minimal context cue and inherited source/date, and stops splitting at the smallest still-unique item
revisit_triggers: a split produces an interference cluster
a residual atom is still graded half-known
the context-cue convention (Rule 16 prefixes) changes

base.update_signal: an interference cluster or a residual-bundle pattern updates the split method

nodes.definition: Define cloze deletion (Wozniak Rule 5): a sentence with a hidden fragment the learner supplies — 'easy and effective,' the fastest path from source text to good items [FACT - snippet]. Anki syntax: wrap hidden text in {{c1::hidden}}; {{c2::...}} and {{c3::...}} on the same note generate SEPARATE cards; holding Alt/Option reuses a number so several blanks hide together; nested clozes are supported from Anki 2.1.56 (depth-limited) [FACT - search snippets of the Anki manual]. Quality guardrails (direct application of Rules 4/11/12, ESTIMATE-high): the deleted span must be SHORT (minimum information); the remaining sentence must UNIQUELY determine the answer (no guessing which of five similar facts); keep the surrounding context meaningful, never a bare list skeleton. Cloze is the workhorse form and the base case for image occlusion.

included: cloze as the base case for occlusion
excluded: image occlusion's image-region specifics
the enumeration overlapping-cloze technique detail

pros.claim: Cloze is the fastest text-to-item form and preserves the surrounding context that keeps an atom unique
pros.example: turning a understood definition sentence into a one-blank cloze in seconds without re-authoring a Q/A pair

cons.claim: Its speed invites bad clozes — long spans, bare list skeletons, or stems that fit several facts — that violate minimum-information and manufacture interference
cons.example: clozing every noun in a sentence so the card has six blanks and no coherent single answer

failure_modes: deleting a long span so the item is no longer atomic
leaving a stem that several similar facts could answer (interference)
clozing a bare list skeleton with no meaningful context
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Rule 5, the {{c1::}}/{{c2::}} separate-card syntax, and the short-span / unique-remainder / meaningful-context guardrails
revisit_triggers: an Anki version changes cloze/nested-cloze behavior
a cloze card shows interference from a non-unique stem
the minimum-span convention is tightened

base.update_signal: an Anki cloze-syntax change or a non-unique-stem interference pattern updates the form

nodes.definition: Define image occlusion (Wozniak Rule 8, graphic deletion): occluding part of an image is 'as good as cloze deletion' — mask one region of an anatomy plate (or map, chart, labeled diagram, flowchart node, table cell) and ask for the missing part [FACT - snippet]. Anki implements it NATIVELY as the Image Occlusion note type since version 23.10 — 'a special case of cloze deletion based on images instead of text' — with rectangles/shapes masking regions, one card per mask or hide-all/reveal-one modes [FACT - search snippets of the Anki manual]. Pre-23.10 the same function was the third-party Image Occlusion Enhanced add-on [FACT that the add-on page exists; authorship an ESTIMATE]. HONESTY: whether occlusion cards outperform equivalent text clozes for a specific domain is [UNKNOWN] — no controlled card-format A/B study was located; the picture-superiority evidence is generic recall, not card-format-specific.

included: the native Image Occlusion note type (Anki >= 23.10) and pre-23.10 add-on
the best-target list and the [UNKNOWN] format-superiority flag
excluded: the general images-vs-text decision (its own node)
the text-cloze syntax detail

pros.claim: Occlusion buys retrieval practice on spatial/labeled knowledge that a text cloze cannot cue as directly
pros.example: masking the apex of a labeled tooth diagram so the learner retrieves the structure from its position

cons.claim: Its advantage over an equivalent text cloze for a specific domain is unproven ([UNKNOWN]), so preferring it must rest on the spatial nature of the knowledge, not a measured card-format win
cons.example: converting a purely verbal number fact into an image-occlusion card for no spatial reason

failure_modes: using occlusion for verbal-symbolic knowledge that a text cloze fits better
claiming occlusion beats text clozes as if a controlled study supported it
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Rule 8, names the native Image Occlusion note type since 23.10 as a cloze-on-images, lists spatial targets, and flags the format-superiority question [UNKNOWN]
revisit_triggers: a controlled occlusion-vs-cloze study is located
an Anki version changes the Image Occlusion note type
a domain's knowledge shifts from spatial to verbal

base.update_signal: an occlusion-vs-cloze study or an Anki note-type change updates the form

nodes.definition: Decide when an image or flowchart beats text (Wozniak Rule 6, use imagery — a picture is worth a thousand words). The evidence: the picture-superiority effect (Paivio: ~twice as many images recalled as words after brief viewing); dual-coding theory (pictures get a visual AND a verbal trace = two retrieval paths) with the caveat that recent work argues distinctiveness, not dual coding, is the mechanism (effect robust, mechanism debated); Mayer's multimedia principle (words + pictures beat words alone) [FACT - search snippets]. Practical rule [ESTIMATE - synthesis, medium-high]: use an image/occlusion card when the knowledge IS spatial or structural (anatomy, apparatus, chart positions); a flowchart occlusion when it is a decision path or sequence; text/cloze when it is verbal-symbolic (definitions, numbers, names). Decorative images add load, not memory — Mayer's coherence principle penalizes extraneous material.

included: Rule 6 and the picture-superiority / dual-coding / multimedia evidence
the spatial->image, decision-path->flowchart, verbal->text decision rule
the coherence-principle penalty on decorative images
excluded: the occlusion note-type mechanics (its own node)
the text-cloze guardrails

pros.claim: A media-choice rule keyed to the KNOWLEDGE type spends the image budget only where a visual trace actually helps recall
pros.example: using a diagram for apparatus layout but a plain cloze for a definition, instead of decorating both

cons.claim: The picture-superiority evidence is generic recall, so it can be over-applied to justify images for verbal facts that gain nothing and cost load
cons.example: adding a stock photo to a numeric definition card and slowing review with no retrieval gain

failure_modes: decorating cards with extraneous images that add load (coherence-principle violation)
using text for genuinely spatial knowledge an image would cue better
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Rule 6 and the picture-superiority/dual-coding/multimedia evidence and gives the spatial->image / decision-path->flowchart / verbal->text rule with the coherence-principle caveat
revisit_triggers: new evidence resolves the dual-coding-vs-distinctiveness mechanism debate
a decorative-image load complaint appears
a domain's knowledge type is reclassified spatial/verbal

base.update_signal: a mechanism-debate resolution or a decorative-load complaint updates the media choice

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rule 12 (optimize wording) and Rule 16 (context cues simplify wording): reduce a card's sentences like equations — compact, minimal-trigger wording speeds recall — and use a short category prefix (e.g. 'chem:', 'bio:') to replace long qualifying phrases AND fight interference by disambiguating otherwise-identical stems [FACT - snippets confirm the concepts; exact Rule 16 heading wording ESTIMATE-high]. This is the lever between a merely-atomic card and a fast, unambiguous one: after a fact is atomized (Rule 4) its stem is tightened until only the intended answer fits, and a context cue is added when a sibling card would otherwise share the stem. It feeds directly into interference control.

included: Rule 12 compact wording and Rule 16 category/context cues
tightening a stem until only the intended answer fits
adding a cue when a sibling would share the stem
excluded: the interference diagnosis and A-vs-B comparison card (its own node)
the atomic split that precedes wording

pros.claim: Compact, cued wording is the cheapest fix that both speeds recall and pre-empts interference before a comparison card is needed
pros.example: prefixing 'ENT:' to a symptom card so it no longer collides with the identical cardiology stem

cons.claim: Over-compressing wording can strip the very context that made the answer unique, tipping a card into ambiguity
cons.example: trimming a stem so hard that two different correct answers now fit it

failure_modes: leaving verbose stems that slow recall and blur the trigger
compressing past the point where the stem uniquely determines the answer
acceptance_tests: the analysis applies Rule 12 compact wording and Rule 16 context cues, tightens the stem to a unique answer, and adds a cue where a sibling shares the stem
revisit_triggers: an ambiguity complaint traces to over-compressed wording
a category-prefix convention is standardized or changed
an interference pair needs a cue not yet defined

base.update_signal: an over-compression ambiguity or a prefix-convention change updates the wording rule

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rule 11 (combat interference): similar items confuse each other and 'even the simplest items can be completely intractable if they are similar to other items' [FACT - snippet]. The crucial property is that interference is a WHOLE-DECK relation, not a per-card defect: a card can be flawless in isolation yet swap answers with one written months later. Diagnosis: two items keep trading answers or one is chronically wrong. Fix set: reword to maximize contrast (Rule 12), add a discriminating context cue (Rule 16), add an explicit A-vs-B comparison card, or delete one item [FACT - Rule 11 diagnosis; the comparison-card fix is common practice, ESTIMATE-medium-high]. This is why the quality gate runs the interference check across the entire deck, not card by card.

included: the reword / cue / comparison-card / delete fix set
excluded: the reversed-card-specific interference case (its own node)
the wording mechanics that a fix reuses

pros.claim: Treating interference as a deck-global property catches the failure the per-card review structurally cannot see
pros.example: flagging two look-alike drug cards that individually pass review but keep swapping in practice

cons.claim: A full-deck interference scan is expensive and grows with deck size, so it is easy to skip and let clusters accumulate
cons.example: adding hundreds of similar cards without re-running the cross-deck check until answers routinely swap

failure_modes: reviewing cards only in isolation and missing cross-deck interference
adding a look-alike card without contrast wording or a discriminating cue
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Rule 11, treats interference as a whole-deck property, gives the trading-answers diagnosis, and lists the reword/cue/comparison-card/delete fixes
revisit_triggers: a swap-pattern surfaces between two cards
the deck grows enough to warrant a re-scan cadence
a new near-duplicate cluster is added

base.update_signal: a swap-pattern or a deck-growth threshold updates the interference control

nodes.definition: Handle the two hardest source shapes (Wozniak Rules 9-10): a SET (unordered collection, 'name the members of X') is 'virtually un-memorizable unless you convert it into an enumeration'; an ENUMERATION (ordered list) is also hard if asked whole and 'can be dealt with using cloze deletion' [FACT - snippets]. The documented chain: set -> impose an order/grouping to make it an enumeration -> cloze each element separately (one blank per card), using overlapping clozes so each item is cued by its neighbors, and Rule 7 mnemonics (peg lists, mind maps) for stubborn orders [FACT - Rules 9/10 snippets; overlapping-cloze technique documented in the Anki community]. Never leave a set or a whole-list card unconverted — it is a guaranteed chronic-lapse item.

included: Rules 9-10 diagnosis of sets and enumerations
overlapping clozes and Rule 7 mnemonics for stubborn orders
excluded: the mnemonic technique detail (its own node)
the generic cloze guardrails

pros.claim: The conversion chain turns an un-memorizable set into a series of accurately-schedulable single-blank items
pros.example: converting 'cranial nerves' from a 12-member set into an ordered, overlapping-cloze enumeration one nerve per card

cons.claim: Imposing an order on a truly unordered set can teach a spurious sequence, and overlapping clozes multiply card count
cons.example: learning an arbitrary order as if it were meaningful and being thrown when the set is queried unordered

failure_modes: leaving a set or whole-list card unconverted so it chronically lapses
over-generating overlapping clozes into an unmanageable card count
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Rules 9-10, gives the set->enumeration->per-element-cloze chain, and names overlapping clozes and Rule 7 mnemonics for stubborn orders
revisit_triggers: a set/enumeration card chronically lapses despite conversion
the overlapping-cloze card count becomes unmanageable
a domain adds a genuinely unordered set

base.update_signal: a chronic-lapse set or an unmanageable overlapping-cloze count updates the conversion

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rule 7 (use mnemonic techniques): peg lists, mind maps and similar devices for otherwise-intractable items — especially stubborn orders that survive the enumeration/cloze conversion [FACT - snippet confirms the rule title]. Mnemonics are the escalation lever, not the default: reach for them only after minimum-information, cloze and enumeration conversion have failed to make an item stick, because a mnemonic adds an extra encoded layer that itself must be maintained. Best fit: fixed arbitrary orders, homophone-prone pairs and lists with no intrinsic logic. This node is the last technique before an item that still will not stick is a candidate for deletion under prioritization.

included: Rule 7 peg lists / mind maps for intractable items
mnemonics as an escalation after cloze/enumeration
excluded: the enumeration conversion that precedes it
the prioritization/deletion decision that follows

pros.claim: A mnemonic rescues the small residue of items that resist every simpler technique without abandoning them
pros.example: a peg-list mnemonic finally fixing an arbitrary 7-item order that overlapping clozes alone did not

cons.claim: Mnemonics add a maintained encoding layer, so over-using them (before simpler fixes) inflates cognitive load for little gain
cons.example: inventing an elaborate mnemonic for a list that a plain cloze would have carried

failure_modes: reaching for a mnemonic before minimum-information and cloze conversion were tried
leaving a truly intractable item unmnemoniced and unprioritized so it lapses forever
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Rule 7, positions mnemonics as an escalation after cloze/enumeration, and names the best-fit intractable targets

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rules 13-15 to bind new items to existing memory: refer to other memories (Rule 13 — anchor new items to what is already known; coherent structure resists forgetting); personalize and provide examples (Rule 14 — personal examples are among the most effective ways to build on existing memories); rely on emotional states (Rule 15 — vivid, personal, even shocking formulations leave stronger traces) [FACT - snippets]. Operationally, each new card should touch a prior item, carry a concrete/personal example, and where natural use a vivid framing. Rule 13 is the direct theoretical basis for edge/relation cards, which are anchoring made structural: every edge card re-binds two already-learned nodes.

included: Rules 13-15 (refer to memories, personalize/examples, emotional states)

excluded: the edge-card mechanics themselves (its own node)

pros.claim: Anchoring each item to prior memory and a personal example makes it far more retention-durable than an isolated fact
pros.example: tying a new pharmacology fact to a remembered case and a vivid example so it resists forgetting

cons.claim: Personal/emotional framing is idiosyncratic and can become interference or noise if the anchor is itself ambiguous or shared
cons.example: a vivid mnemonic image reused across several cards so the images now collide

failure_modes: shipping isolated facts with no anchor to prior items (orphan risk)

acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Rules 13-15, requires each card to anchor to a prior item with a concrete example, and names Rule 13 as the edge-card basis

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rules 18-19 as the honesty layer: provide sources (Rule 18 — source annotations let you update knowledge and judge its reliability later) and provide date stamping (Rule 19 — stamp volatile facts, especially statistics, with their collection year to manage obsolescence) [FACT - snippets]. House policy for this factory [ESTIMATE - house design decision]: every generated card carries its KB source id, so a card is traceable to the claim/edge it came from and to that claim's honesty tag ([FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN]); volatile facts (statistics, prices, guidelines, version numbers like 'Anki 23.10') also carry a date. An undated volatile fact silently goes stale — the documented failure of the 'undated volatile fact' bad-card pattern.

included: the house KB-source-id-per-card policy and honesty-tag inheritance
excluded: the bad-card taxonomy entry that consumes this (its own node)

pros.example: a statistic card stamped with its year and KB id so a later fetch can correct and re-date it

nodes.definition: Apply Wozniak Rule 20 (prioritize): you will always face more knowledge than you can master, so choose deliberately what to card [FACT - snippet]. This is the meta-lever that stops the pipeline from carding every atomizable fact just because it CAN: high-value, high-frequency knowledge (the heavily-indexed hub terms, the exam-relevant claims) is carded first; low-value trivia is deferred or dropped even if it would make a clean card. It also governs the disposal of an item that resists every technique and mnemonic — an intractable low-priority item is a legitimate delete. Prioritization is a lens the final go/no-go applies, balancing coverage against the reviewer's finite time budget.

excluded: the coverage validation against source questions (in the go/no-go node)

pros.claim: Explicit prioritization protects the reviewer's finite time by spending it on high-value knowledge instead of exhaustively carding trivia
pros.example: carding the hub terms and exam-relevant claims first and deferring rarely-tested footnotes

cons.claim: Prioritization pulls against exhaustive coverage, so an over-aggressive cut can drop material the source's own questions later demand

failure_modes: carding every atomizable fact and drowning the reviewer in low-value items

nodes.definition: Map each fact shape to an Anki note template. Basic (Front->Back, one card): a one-directional fact ('What nerve innervates X?') [FACT - Anki manual snippet]. Basic (and reversed card): generates Front->Back AND Back->Front, for symmetric pairs like term<->definition or drug<->class [FACT - snippet]. Basic (optional reversed card): a reverse only when an 'Add Reverse' field is non-empty, for pairs where only SOME deserve a reverse [FACT on the mechanism; exact type name ESTIMATE-high]. Basic (type in the answer): learner types, diffed against the field, for spellings/terminology [ESTIMATE - training knowledge of the manual, not snippet-confirmed this session]. Cloze: {{c1::...}} deletions for facts embedded in sentences and enumerations [FACT - snippet]. Image Occlusion: masks over image regions for diagrams/anatomy (Anki >= 23.10) [FACT - snippet]. Choose the SIMPLEST template that carries the atom.

included: which template facts are snippet-confirmed vs training-knowledge
excluded: the reversed-card uniqueness discipline (its own node)
the edge-card family

pros.claim: A fact-shape-to-template map removes guesswork and stops a symmetric pair being authored as two hand-made one-directional cards
pros.example: using Basic-and-reversed for a term/definition pair instead of writing two separate cards that can drift

cons.claim: Some template facts (optional-reversed name, type-in) are training-knowledge not snippet-confirmed this session, so the map must flag that uncertainty rather than assert the manual
cons.example: stating the exact 'optional reversed' type name as authoritative when only its mechanism was confirmed

failure_modes: choosing an over-complex template (reversed/occlusion) when a Basic or Cloze carries the atom

acceptance_tests: the analysis maps each fact shape to a template, prefers the simplest template that carries the atom, and flags the snippet-confirmed vs training-knowledge status of each

nodes.definition: Govern when auto-reversing is safe: only auto-reverse a card when the BACK uniquely identifies the front [ESTIMATE - standard practice + Rule 11, high confidence]. A reversed card whose 'question' is a generic definition shared by several terms manufactures interference — the back cues many possible fronts, so the item becomes intractable. Decision procedure: if the back is a unique identifier (a proper name, a specific value), use Basic-and-reversed; if the back is a generic phrase some other card also uses, either suppress the reverse (plain Basic) or use Basic-optional-reversed and only fill the reverse field for the unambiguous ones. This is the interference-control rule specialized to the reversing mechanism, and a mandatory check in the lint gate.

included: reversing as a specialized interference case
excluded: the general interference fixes (its own node)
the template catalog

pros.claim: A uniqueness test on the reverse captures the retrieval value of bidirectional recall without silently seeding interference
pros.example: auto-reversing a drug<->unique-mechanism pair but not a term<->generic-definition pair

cons.claim: Suppressing reverses to avoid interference forgoes some bidirectional practice, so a blanket no-reverse policy under-trains genuinely symmetric pairs
cons.example: never reversing any card and losing the back->front recall on truly unique pairs

failure_modes: auto-reversing a card whose generic back is shared by several fronts (manufactured interference)
blanket-suppressing all reverses and under-training symmetric unique pairs
acceptance_tests: the analysis states auto-reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front, gives the suppress-or-optional-reverse decision, and frames it as a specialized interference case
revisit_triggers: a reversed card shows interference from a shared back
a symmetric-pair convention changes
the interference fix set is updated

base.update_signal: a shared-back interference case or a symmetric-pair convention change updates the rule

nodes.definition: Build edge (relation) cards from the owner's 'edges' — read as concept-map propositions (Novak & Canas 2008: two concepts joined by linking words into a meaningful statement) [FACT that propositions are defined that way; the edges=propositions reading is ESTIMATE-high]. An edge is a triple (A, relation, B), e.g. (lidocaine, blocks, Na+ channels) or (maxillary first molar, has-root-count, 3). Each triple yields a small card family [ESTIMATE - design synthesis]: (1) forward 'What does A <relation>?' -> B; (2) reverse 'What <relation> B?' -> A, ONLY if unique (Rule 11 / reversed discipline); (3) relation card 'How are A and B related?' -> the linking phrase; (4) cloze 'A <relation> {{c1::B}}.'. Edge cards ARE the Rule 13 mechanism in card form — each touches two already-learned nodes and re-binds the graph. HARD PRECONDITION: an edge card is well-formed only after BOTH endpoint term-cards exist.

included: the both-endpoints-must-exist precondition and the Rule 13 link
excluded: how edges are extracted from the book (the decomposition KB)
the reversed-card uniqueness rule detail

pros.claim: Edge cards operationalize Rule 13 structurally, so every review re-binds two nodes and builds the relational layer exams actually test
pros.example: a (drug, blocks, channel) edge family that keeps the two endpoint concepts wired together across reviews

cons.claim: An edge card authored before both endpoint term-cards exist is an orphan that tests an unlearned node
cons.example: asking 'what does lidocaine block?' before the learner has a Na+-channel term card

failure_modes: authoring an edge card before both endpoint term-cards exist (orphan)
auto-generating the reverse of an edge whose B is non-unique (interference)
acceptance_tests: the analysis reads edges as (A, relation, B) propositions, gives the four-card family with reverse-only-if-unique, and enforces the both-endpoints-exist precondition tied to Rule 13

base.update_signal: an edge-orphan case or an extraction-format change updates the edge-card build

nodes.definition: Catalog the documented bad-card failure patterns with their Rule-anchored fixes: OVERLOADED (violates Rule 4; many sub-answers, one grade) -> split into atoms, keep redundancy per Rule 17; SET (unordered, un-memorizable) -> convert to enumeration then clozes (Rules 9/10); ENUMERATION (whole list asked) -> cloze each element, overlapping clozes, mnemonics; INTERFERENCE PAIR (two similar items swap answers) -> reword for contrast, add context cue (Rule 16), add A-vs-B comparison card, sometimes delete one; AMBIGUOUS QUESTION (many correct answers, one accepted) -> tighten wording until unique (Rule 12); ORPHAN (fact with no understood context) -> learn the chapter first, link to prior items (Rule 13), add an example (Rule 14); UNDATED VOLATILE FACT -> date-stamp (Rule 19) and source-stamp (Rule 18) [FACT on the Rule anchors per snippets; the comparison-card and KB-id fixes are ESTIMATE/house-practice]. This taxonomy is the checklist the lint gate runs.

excluded: running the checklist over the deck (the lint gate node)
the individual technique mechanics each fix reuses

pros.claim: A named taxonomy turns 'this card feels bad' into a diagnosable pattern with a specific documented fix
pros.example: recognizing a swap as an interference pair and reaching for the comparison-card fix instead of guessing

cons.claim: Some fixes (comparison card, KB-id policy) are common practice not snippet-verbatim, so the taxonomy must mark which fixes are the article's and which are house practice
cons.example: presenting the A-vs-B comparison-card fix as Wozniak's own wording when it is common practice

failure_modes: mis-diagnosing a pattern and applying the wrong fix
presenting a house-practice fix as verbatim Wozniak

nodes.definition: Run the bad-card taxonomy as a deck-level lint pass before cards ship, applying each documented fix: split overloaded cards to atoms (Rule 4/17); convert sets -> enumerations -> clozes (Rules 9/10); tighten ambiguous wording to a unique answer (Rule 12); anchor orphans to prior items with an example (Rules 13/14); source- and date-stamp volatile facts (Rules 18/19); enforce uniqueness on every reversed and edge-reverse card; and — critically — run the interference check across the WHOLE deck, not card by card, because Rule 11 is a global property. A card that fails any check loops back to re-splitting or re-wording rather than shipping. This is the gate that makes the abstract rules an enforced pipeline stage.

excluded: the final coverage/honesty go/no-go verdict (its own node)
the taxonomy definitions themselves

failure_modes: running the interference check per-card instead of across the whole deck

acceptance_tests: the gate applies the split/convert/tighten/anchor/stamp/uniqueness fixes, runs the interference check across the whole deck, and loops any failure back to re-split/re-word
revisit_triggers: a shipped defect reveals a missing lint check

a taxonomy fix is added or changed

base.update_signal: a shipped defect or a deck-scale change updates the lint gate

nodes.definition: Compose the ship/no-ship verdict the whole KB builds toward: a card (and the deck) is a GO when it clears every binding gate simultaneously — (1) minimum-information: it is one atomic fact, overloaded cards split (Rule 4/17); (2) interference: it passes the whole-deck contrast check (Rule 11); (3) form fit: the simplest template carries it, reversed/edge-reverse cards are unique; (4) sets/enumerations converted (Rules 9/10); (5) anchoring/honesty: it touches a prior item, carries a source id and, if volatile, a date (Rules 13/18/19); (6) prioritization: it is worth the reviewer's time (Rule 20); and (7) traceability: it maps to a claim/edge, and the deck can answer the source's own end-of-chapter questions. A card that is atomic but interferes, or clean but orphaned, or volatile but undated, is a NO-GO until the failing gate is cleared — failures loop back to the lint gate.

excluded: the per-rule mechanics (their own nodes)

failure_modes: shipping a card on one passing gate while another is failing

acceptance_tests: the verdict conjoins minimum-information, interference, form fit, set/enumeration conversion, anchoring/honesty, prioritization and traceability, and loops any failure back to the lint gate
revisit_triggers: a source update changes a claim a card traces to

base.update_signal: a source update, a new sibling card, or a coverage miss changes the ship verdict

conflict_axes.name: atomicity_vs_disambiguating_context
conflict_axes.description: Splitting an item to the smallest atom (Rule 4) removes context, but the remaining stem must still uniquely determine the answer (Rule 11), so atomization and disambiguation pull against each other.
poles: keep enough context to stay unique
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split only until the stem still uniquely determines the answer, then add a minimal context cue (Rule 16) rather than splitting further

conflict_axes.name: minimum_information_vs_redundancy
conflict_axes.description: Rule 4 wants the fewest, simplest items while Rule 17 welcomes the same fact from several angles, so authors must place the line between necessary redundancy and bloat.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep redundancy only as separate SIMPLE items that each add a distinct retrieval angle; never as a single compound card

conflict_axes.name: image_value_vs_extraneous_load
conflict_axes.description: The picture-superiority effect argues for images while Mayer's coherence principle penalizes decorative/extraneous images that add working-memory load.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reserve images/occlusion for spatial or structural knowledge and strip decorative images that do not carry the atom

conflict_axes.name: auto_reverse_coverage_vs_interference
conflict_axes.description: Auto-reversing a card doubles bidirectional recall but a generic, shared back cues many fronts and manufactures interference.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: auto-reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front; use optional-reversed for the mixed case

conflict_axes.name: enumeration_wholesale_vs_clozed_elements
conflict_axes.description: Asking a list whole is one card but forces long serial recall with uneven mastery, while clozing each element multiplies cards but schedules each item honestly.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: convert the list to per-element overlapping clozes and reserve mnemonics for orders that still resist

conflict_axes.name: verbatim_authority_vs_reconstructed_source
conflict_axes.description: The Twenty Rules' exact wording was 403-blocked and reconstructed from snippets, so presenting a rule as verbatim canon pulls against carrying the reconstruction honestly.
poles: present the gloss as canonical wording
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state the rule's CONCEPT (snippet-confirmed) and flag verbatim wording as reconstructed/[UNKNOWN] until fetch access confirms it

conflict_axes.name: exhaustive_coverage_vs_prioritized_time
conflict_axes.description: The deck must answer the source's own questions (coverage) while Rule 20 prioritization protects the reviewer's finite time, so coverage and prioritization compete.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prioritize high-value/high-frequency knowledge first but keep enough to answer the source's end-of-chapter questions

conflict_axes.name: cloze_authoring_speed_vs_card_quality
conflict_axes.description: Cloze is the fastest text-to-item form (Rule 5), but that speed produces long-span, bare-skeleton, non-unique clozes unless the lint gate catches them.
poles: hold every card to the lint gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: author fast but pass every cloze through the short-span/unique-remainder/meaningful-context guardrails and the deck lint before shipping

conflict_axes.name: local_card_soundness_vs_global_deck_property
conflict_axes.description: A card can be flawless in isolation yet interfere with a card written months later, because Rule 11 interference is a whole-deck relation not a per-card defect.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the interference and uniqueness checks across the entire deck at the gate, not only when the card is authored

edge_cases.description: A card is atomic and well-worded but swaps answers with a look-alike card added months later
edge_cases.trigger: a new near-duplicate card enters the deck without a cross-deck interference re-scan
edge_cases.mitigation: run the interference check across the whole deck on each batch, and reword for contrast or add an A-vs-B comparison card when two items swap

edge_cases.description: An overloaded card is split into atoms that all share an identical bare stem and now form an interference cluster
edge_cases.trigger: the split drops the disambiguating context (Rule 16 cue) from each child
edge_cases.mitigation: stop splitting at the smallest still-unique item and add a minimal category/context cue to each atom

edge_cases.description: A cloze deletes a long multi-clause span so the item is no longer atomic and is chronically half-known
edge_cases.trigger: cloze authoring speed outruns the short-span guardrail
edge_cases.mitigation: restrict each deletion to a short span and split multi-clause clozes into separate one-blank cards

edge_cases.description: A reversed card's generic definition back is shared by several terms, so the reverse cues many possible fronts
edge_cases.trigger: Basic-and-reversed is used on a term whose definition is not a unique identifier
edge_cases.mitigation: auto-reverse only when the back uniquely identifies the front; otherwise suppress the reverse or use optional-reversed

edge_cases.description: An edge card asks 'what does A relate to?' before the learner has a term card for the endpoint B
edge_cases.trigger: an edge is compiled before both endpoint term-cards exist
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the precondition that both endpoint term-cards exist before an edge card is well-formed

edge_cases.description: A set ('name the members of X') is carded whole and chronically lapses
edge_cases.trigger: a set is left unconverted to an enumeration and clozes
edge_cases.mitigation: impose an order/grouping to make it an enumeration, then cloze each element with overlapping clozes

edge_cases.description: A volatile fact (a statistic, price, or a version note like 'Anki 23.10') is carded without a date and silently goes stale
edge_cases.trigger: the date-stamp check (Rule 19) is skipped in the lint pass
edge_cases.mitigation: date-stamp every volatile fact and source-stamp it with its KB id so it can be re-checked and re-dated

edge_cases.description: A rule's exact wording is quoted verbatim on a card as authoritative when only the concept was snippet-confirmed this session
edge_cases.trigger: the reconstructed-text honesty flag is dropped when the rule is turned into a card
edge_cases.mitigation: card the rule's concept, mark verbatim wording as reconstructed/[UNKNOWN], and carry the source id so a later fetch can correct it

edge_cases.description: An image-occlusion card is made for a purely verbal-symbolic fact that a text cloze would carry better
edge_cases.trigger: occlusion is chosen for a non-spatial fact on the assumption it beats text
edge_cases.mitigation: use occlusion only for spatial/structural knowledge; the occlusion-vs-cloze advantage for a specific domain is [UNKNOWN], so default to text cloze for verbal facts

edge_cases.description: A decorative image is added to a definition card and slows review with no retrieval gain
edge_cases.trigger: an image is added for engagement rather than because the knowledge is spatial
edge_cases.mitigation: strip extraneous images (coherence principle) and keep only images that carry the atom

edge_cases.description: Every atomizable fact in a chapter is carded, drowning the reviewer, while a topic the source's own questions test is missing
edge_cases.trigger: exhaustive extraction runs without a prioritization or coverage check
edge_cases.mitigation: prioritize high-value knowledge first (Rule 20) but verify the deck still answers the source's end-of-chapter questions

workflow.gate: each item is one atomic fact with the single-trace rationale and the Rule 17 complement stated

workflow.action: Choose the form: cloze, occlusion or image
workflow.description: Apply cloze with its guardrails, use occlusion for image regions, and the image-vs-text rule
workflow.gate: cloze guardrails (short span, unique remainder, meaningful context) and the spatial-vs-verbal media rule are applied

workflow.description: Tighten wording (Rule 12), add context cues (Rule 16), and run the whole-deck interference check
workflow.gate: wording is compact/unique and interference is checked across the whole deck with the fix set

workflow.description: Turn sets into enumerations and enumerations into per-element overlapping clozes, mnemonics for stubborn orders
workflow.gate: no set or whole-list card remains; each element is a single-blank cloze

workflow.action: Anchor items and choose the note template
workflow.description: Anchor each item to prior memory (Rules 13-15) and map its shape to the simplest Anki template
workflow.gate: each card is anchored and assigned the simplest template that carries it, with note-type honesty flags

workflow.action: Build edge cards under the uniqueness and endpoint rules
workflow.description: Compile (A, relation, B) card families, reversing only when unique and only after both endpoints exist
workflow.gate: edge families are well-formed with reverse-only-if-unique and both endpoint term-cards present

workflow.description: Attach a KB source id to every card and a date to every volatile fact (Rules 18-19)
workflow.gate: every card carries a source id and every volatile fact a date, inheriting the source honesty tag

workflow.description: Apply the taxonomy's fixes over the deck and loop failures back to re-split/re-word
workflow.gate: the split/convert/tighten/anchor/stamp/uniqueness fixes and the whole-deck interference scan are applied, failures loop back

workflow.description: Conjoin all gates plus prioritization and source-question coverage into a ship verdict
workflow.gate: the verdict conjoins minimum-info, interference, form fit, conversion, anchoring/honesty, prioritization and coverage/traceability

dominance_rules.rationale: a card cut from un-understood text is an orphan that lapses forever (Rules 1-3)
dominance_rules.trigger: a card is being compiled from material not yet understood
dominance_rules.action: run the reading/understanding pass first and only then compile cards

dominance_rules.rule: The minimum-information principle dominates authoring convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: the scheduler grades a single memory trace, so a bundled card is graded meaninglessly (Rule 4)
dominance_rules.trigger: an item carries more than one atomic fact
dominance_rules.action: split it into atoms, keeping redundancy only as separate simple items (Rule 17)

dominance_rules.rule: The whole-deck interference check dominates per-card review
dominance_rules.rationale: interference is a global property; a card fine in isolation can swap answers with a distant one (Rule 11)
dominance_rules.trigger: a card is being approved on its own merits
dominance_rules.action: run the interference/uniqueness check across the entire deck before approving

dominance_rules.rationale: a generic shared back cues many fronts and manufactures interference
dominance_rules.trigger: auto-reverse is applied to a card whose back is not a unique identifier
dominance_rules.action: suppress the reverse or use optional-reversed and fill only the unambiguous ones

dominance_rules.rationale: an edge card tests two nodes, so it is an orphan if either endpoint term-card is missing
dominance_rules.trigger: an edge (A, relation, B) is being carded
dominance_rules.action: require both endpoint term-cards to exist before authoring the edge family

dominance_rules.rule: Set/enumeration conversion dominates carding a list whole
dominance_rules.rationale: sets are un-memorizable and whole enumerations force serial recall (Rules 9-10)
dominance_rules.trigger: a set or ordered list is about to be carded as one item
dominance_rules.action: convert set -> enumeration -> per-element overlapping clozes before shipping

dominance_rules.rule: The date/source stamp dominates the raw volatile fact
dominance_rules.rationale: an undated volatile fact silently goes stale and cannot be audited (Rules 18-19)
dominance_rules.trigger: a statistic, price, guideline or version note is carded
dominance_rules.action: attach a date and a KB source id carrying the fact's honesty tag

dominance_rules.rule: Knowledge-type dominates the decision to add an image
dominance_rules.rationale: picture superiority helps spatial knowledge but decorative images add load (coherence principle)
dominance_rules.trigger: an image is being added to a card
dominance_rules.action: add the image only when the knowledge is spatial/structural and it carries the atom; otherwise use text/cloze

dominance_rules.rationale: the reviewer's time is finite and more knowledge exists than can be mastered (Rule 20)
dominance_rules.trigger: every atomizable fact is being carded regardless of value
dominance_rules.action: card high-value/high-frequency knowledge first, subject to answering the source's own questions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the comprehension pass before compiling any card from a unit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: orphan rote cards that must be deleted and re-learned once the material is finally understood

anti_rework_rules.rule: Atomize to one fact and add a context cue at authoring time, not after a lapse
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking a whole batch of overloaded or colliding cards once they show up as half-known

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the short-span / unique-remainder cloze guardrails as each cloze is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-cutting long-span, bare-skeleton clozes into atomic items after they fail in review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Test back-uniqueness before enabling auto-reverse on a note type
anti_rework_rules.prevents: seeding a deck-wide interference cluster that must later be diagnosed and un-reversed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm both endpoint term-cards exist before authoring an edge card
anti_rework_rules.prevents: orphan edge cards that test an unlearned node and have to be pulled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Convert sets and enumerations at extraction time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: chronically-lapsing whole-list cards that must be rebuilt as clozes after they fail

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stamp source id and date on a card when it is created
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an un-auditable deck of stale, unattributed facts that must be re-sourced later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the whole-deck interference scan per batch, not once at the end
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a late, expensive full-deck de-interference pass after swap pairs have accumulated

iteration_protocol.trigger: fetch access to supermemo.com / the Anki manual is restored and verbatim rule text or the note-type list is confirmed
iteration_protocol.action: replace the reconstructed wording, clear the verbatim [UNKNOWN] flag, and correct any rule position or template name

iteration_protocol.trigger: a controlled study comparing image-occlusion cards to equivalent text clozes for a domain is located
iteration_protocol.action: update the media-choice rule and the occlusion node with the measured format effect

iteration_protocol.trigger: a recurring bad-card pattern not in the taxonomy is observed in the deck
iteration_protocol.action: add the pattern and its fix to the taxonomy and the lint gate checklist

iteration_protocol.trigger: the deck fails to answer some of the source's end-of-chapter questions (a coverage miss)
iteration_protocol.action: loop back to prioritization and re-extract the missing claims/edges, then re-run the go/no-go

iteration_protocol.trigger: a swap pattern between two cards surfaces in review logs
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the whole-deck interference check and apply the reword/cue/comparison-card/delete fix

iteration_protocol.trigger: the book-decomposition KB changes the claim/edge extraction format the cards consume
iteration_protocol.action: update the edge-card build and the atomic-split inputs to the new format

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new Anki version changes cloze, nested-cloze or Image Occlusion behavior
iteration_protocol.action: update the cloze and occlusion nodes and re-date the version-stamped cards

priority_rationale: The testing-effect warrant, the Twenty Rules canon and the comprehension gate come first because every formulation technique serves retrieval accuracy and presupposes understood source material; the minimum-information principle, the atomic-split method, cloze, occlusion, the image-vs-text choice and wording/interference control next, because they are the core techniques that turn an understood fact into a well-formed item; sets/enumerations, mnemonics, anchoring, source/date stamping and prioritization then add the harder-shape and meta-management rules; template selection, reversed-card discipline and edge cards apply all of this to concrete Anki note types; and the bad-card taxonomy, the deck-level lint gate and the merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream rule into an enforced deck-scope quality verdict.
